canvas.$description: The app background, behind every surface. Not for cards, panels or menus: use color.bg.surface, raised or overlay.

surface.$description: Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs that sit on the canvas. Not for floating layers: use color.bg.raised (popovers, dropdowns) or color.bg.overlay (dialogs).

raised.$description: Layers that float above a surface: popovers, dropdown menus, tooltips. Not for content that scrolls with the page: use color.bg.surface.

overlay.$description: The top layer: dialogs, drawers, command palettes. Not for the dimmed backdrop behind a dialog, and not for ordinary cards.

inset.$description: Recessed areas inside a surface: wells, code blocks, secondary buttons, table headers. Not a hover state: use color.interactive.hover.

default.$description: Body text, headings and icons that carry meaning. Not for text on a solid accent or status background: use color.fg.on-accent.

muted.$description: Secondary text: labels, descriptions, captions, inactive tabs. Not for disabled content (use color.fg.disabled) and not for body text.

subtle.$description: Tertiary text: placeholders, hints, timestamps, decorative icons. Not for anything the user must read to complete a task: use color.fg.muted or default.

disabled.$description: Text and icons of disabled controls. Never for readable content: it is below text contrast on purpose (WCAG exempts disabled controls).

link.$description: Hyperlinks and link-styled buttons in running text. Not for emphasis and not on a solid accent background.

on-accent.$description: Text and icons on color.accent.bg and on solid status backgrounds. Not on neutral backgrounds: use color.fg.default.

default.$description: Separators and the outline of cards, panels and table cells. Not the only cue that identifies a control (it is below 3:1): use color.border.strong.

strong.$description: The outline that identifies a control: inputs, checkboxes, outlined buttons (at least 3:1). Not for separators between content: use color.border.default.

ring.$description: The focus ring of any focusable element. Not a decorative border and not a selection colour: use color.interactive.selected.

bg.$description: The filled background of the primary action and of checked controls. Not for large areas, and not more than one primary action per view.

bg-hover.$description: color.accent.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.

bg-active.$description: color.accent.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.

subtle-bg.$description: A tinted background for accent badges, tags and highlighted callouts. Not for the selected row or item: use color.interactive.selected.

subtle-fg.$description: Text and icons on color.accent.subtle-bg. Not on color.accent.bg: use color.fg.on-accent.

hover.$description: A translucent wash over any background for hovered rows, menu items and ghost buttons. Not for filled controls: use the role's own hover token (color.accent.bg-hover).

active.$description: The same wash while pressed. Not for a persistent selected state: use color.interactive.selected.

selected.$description: A translucent accent wash for the selected row, item or tab. Not for hover, and not for text selection inside an editor.

solid.$description: The filled background of a destructive action, and the border of an invalid field. Not for error text on a neutral background: use color.status.danger.fg.

solid-hover.$description: color.status.danger.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

fg.$description: Text and icons for errors and destructive actions, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.danger.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

bg.$description: A tinted background for errors and destructive actions: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

fg.$description: Text and icons for warnings that need attention but do not block, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.warning.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

bg.$description: A tinted background for warnings that need attention but do not block: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

fg.$description: Text and icons for success and completion, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.success.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

bg.$description: A tinted background for success and completion: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

fg.$description: Text and icons for neutral information, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.info.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

bg.$description: A tinted background for neutral information: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

sm.$description: Small elements: checkboxes, tags, extra-small controls. Not for standard controls: use radius.md.

md.$description: Standard controls: buttons, inputs, menu items. Not for containers: use radius.lg.

lg.$description: Containers: cards, popovers, dialogs. Not for controls inside those containers: use radius.md.

sans.$description: All interface text. Not for code, identifiers or tabular data that must align: use font.mono.

mono.$description: Code, SQL, identifiers, and grid cells that must align. Not for labels or prose.

raised.$description: The lift of buttons and cards one step above their background. Not for popovers or dialogs, which need a deeper shadow.

xs.$description: Height of the smallest controls: inline tags, icon buttons inside a row. Not a touch target; not for primary actions.

sm.$description: Height of small controls and of dense rows (toolbars, grid rows). Not for forms a user fills in at length: use size.control.md.

md.$description: Height of standard controls: buttons, inputs, selects. Not a fixed pixel value: never hard-code 36px, the density mode changes it.

lg.$description: Height of large controls: the main call to action, touch-first layouts. Not inside dense tools such as grids and toolbars.

x.$description: Horizontal padding inside a standard control. Not for gaps between controls or for layout spacing.
